articles.title: SJAA EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: The document, titled "SJAA EPHEMERIS," is the official publication of the San Jose Astronomical Association. This specific issue is Volume 5, Number 2, released in February 1994.

articles.title: The Eyepiece
articles.summary: This newsletter column, 'The Eyepiece,' provides updates on club activities, including a review of a past speaker from MIRA and announcements for upcoming general meetings featuring Paul Graves. It lists numerous star parties and observational astronomy classes, along with reminders about the Julian Day calendar and an obituary for Walter Scott Houston. The article also touches on newsletter advertising and solicits plans for viewing an annular eclipse in May.

articles.title: Here's something for the PC owner
articles.summary: This article announces the immediate availability of version 2 of "SkyMap," a popular Windows 3.1 shareware astronomy program. SkyMap can accurately map the sky, display various celestial objects, and print high-quality charts, with its accuracy comparable to the "Astronomical Almanac." New features in this release include a significant speed increase, a customizable comet catalog, and the addition of Pluto.

articles.title: Walter Scott Huston
articles.summary: Walter Scott Huston, widely known as "Scotty" and author of Sky & Telescope's Deep Sky Wonders column since 1946, passed away on December 23rd at age 81 from pneumonia in Cancun, Mexico. A highly influential figure in amateur astronomy, he was celebrated for his deep sky and variable star observations, his contributions to AAVSO, and his long-standing presence at Stellafane conventions. His passion for astronomy, ignited in childhood, inspired generations of enthusiasts.

articles.title: More IBM Shareware available
articles.summary: The article announces the release of STARPLOT V2.0, an IBM shareware drawing package specifically designed for creating star charts. It is now available for download from the SimTel Software Repository via anonymous FTP from OAK.Oakland.Edu and its mirror sites.

articles.title: Sky Map (Continued from page 1)
articles.summary: This article describes two astronomy software programs: SkyMap and Starplot v2.0. SkyMap is a shareware program for Windows offering object search, map orientation adjustments for telescopes, global location settings, and a comprehensive star/object catalog suitable for both novice and serious amateur astronomers. Starplot v2.0 is a star chart drawing package that allows users to plot celestial objects, create detailed finder charts from Hubble GSC data, and import planet, minor planet, and comet positions via its Makeplan.exe utility.

articles.title: Shuttle Launch and Paload schedule
articles.summary: This document outlines the Space Shuttle launch schedule for missions from January 1994 to May 1995, detailing specific mission numbers (e.g., STS-60 to STS-71), launch dates, orbital inclinations, and primary payloads. Additionally, it includes an important notice regarding the availability of electronic still camera images of the Hubble Space Telescope from the STS-61 mission, accessible via an FTP server.

articles.title: Moon Calculations
articles.summary: A user seeks a simple program to calculate the Moon's angular position from Earth given location and time. The response explains that these calculations are complex, recommending the 'xephem' lunar code for reasonable accuracy or high-precision N-body ephemeris data from the US Naval Observatory for professional-grade work, which requires extensive coding and consideration of relativistic effects and Earth's motion.

articles.title: Product Manager
articles.summary: Orion Telescope Center is seeking an experienced Product Manager with a strong technical or engineering background for a senior position. The role requires a seasoned amateur astronomer with substantial telescope experience, excellent familiarity with optical and mechanical design, and broad knowledge of commercial telescopes and accessories. Responsibilities include new product design and product line development.

articles.title: Bolide Meteor
articles.summary: A bright bolide meteor was reported to have been observed on Saturday, January 8, 1994, at 5:34 local time, from Selkirk and Clandeboye, Manitoba, Canada. Chris Rutkowski of the University of Manitoba disseminated the report and requested further observations or posts from anyone who witnessed the event.

articles.title: Here is a quick, easy and CHEAP focusing aid:
articles.summary: This article provides detailed instructions for constructing a quick, easy, and cheap focusing aid, primarily for Schmidt-Cassegrain Telescopes (SCTs), using a 12"x12" piece of 1/8" aircraft modeling plywood. The process involves tracing the telescope's aperture, marking specific points, cutting two precisely placed holes, adding small wooden holders, and spray-painting the entire device flat black for optimal performance.

articles.title: DIRECTIONS FOR USE:
articles.summary: This document provides simple, five-step instructions for using a homemade telescope focuser, which was created by the author as an inexpensive alternative to commercially available devices. It describes how to achieve precise focus by merging a double image of a celestial object. The author, Dennis Ward of the Birmingham Astronomical Society, shares his DIY solution for improved astrophotography.

articles.title: More Astro Ad(s)
articles.summary: This document is a classified advertisement listing various used astronomical equipment for sale. Items include a Meade 8" f/6 Newtonian telescope with accessories, a Celestron C90 Spotting Scope, Lumicon filters, Meade eyepieces, and other components, offered with individual and package pricing.

articles.title: Here is another CHEAP Telescope Tool suggested by 'CRAZY Ed' Erbeck
articles.summary: This article details how to construct a budget-friendly Newtonian telescope collimation tool, inspired by 'CRAZY Ed' Erbeck. It involves using a Kodak 35mm film canister with adhesive aluminum tape and a central hole, along with marking the primary mirror's center. The device is then used to align the primary mirror by centering the marked dot within the tool's hole, assuming the secondary mirror is already aligned.

articles.title: NOTICE
articles.summary: This notice announces the upcoming election for four Board of Director members. It lists four current members running for re-election and provides instructions for nominating additional candidates either in advance by contacting specific individuals or from the floor at the February general meeting.

articles.title: Directions to our Favorite Places
articles.summary: This article provides detailed directions to several key locations for an astronomy club's activities, welcoming both members and the public. It includes directions to Milpitas Library for general meetings, Houge Park for observational astronomy classes and public star parties, Henry Coe State Park for scheduled star parties, and Grant Ranch for observing, outlining activities, times, and specific site rules for each.

articles.title: REMEMBER THAT ENTERING GRANT RANCH AFTER 10:00 P.M. CAN BE DANGEROUS TO YOUR AUTOMOBILE TIRES. DO NOT GO THROUGH THE EXIT GATE WHEN THE ENTRANCE IS LOCKED!
articles.summary: This article issues a safety warning about dangerous conditions for automobile tires when entering Grant Ranch after 10:00 P.M. or attempting to exit through a locked entrance. It also provides the 1994 calendar for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), listing dates for general meetings, Houge Park Star Parties, and observational astronomy classes from February to July.

articles.title: Telescope Loaner Status
articles.summary: This document provides an update on the status of a telescope loaner program, listing various telescopes, their current users, due dates, and availability. Several telescopes, including a 4-1/2" Newt/P mount, 6" Dobson, 12-1/2" Dobson, 6" Newt/P mount, and another 6" Newt/P mount, are currently available. Members interested in borrowing a telescope or getting on a waiting list are instructed to contact Paul Barton, with special conditions noted for the solar telescope.

articles.title: ASTRO ADS
articles.summary: This document, titled "ASTRO ADS," serves as a classifieds section for noncommercial advertisers to sell or seek astronomically related products and services. It provides submission guidelines, including an editor's contact information and monthly deadlines, and features numerous listings for used telescopes, mounts, cameras, filters, magazines, and other astronomical equipment.

articles.title: February 1994
articles.summary: This document provides an astronomical guide for February 1994, detailing lunar phases with their rise, transit, and set times. It also includes observational data for Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn, listing their positions, magnitudes, and visibility times. Further information covers solar data, astronomical twilight times, sidereal time, and a specific recommendation for the darkest Saturday night on February 5th, making it a comprehensive monthly sky planner.

articles.title: TIMES AND DATES ARE PACIFIC DAYLIGHT
articles.summary: This document specifies that all listed times and dates are in Pacific Daylight Time (PDT). It also notes that planet distance and magnitude values, provided for the 17th of each month, are derived from 'Astronomy with Your Personal Computer' by Peter Duffet-Smith and 'MacEphem' by Elwood Charles Downey.

articles.title: Offices and Board of Directors
articles.summary: This document provides a directory of key personnel and their contact information for an organization. It lists the President, Treasurer, Secretary, and Board of Directors, along with individuals contributing to the Ephemeris and the Editor, each with their respective phone numbers.

articles.title: Comet Comments
articles.summary: This article provides updates on various comets, noting the departure of Comets Encke and Mueller, and anticipating Comet Shoemaker-Levy 9's impending impact with Jupiter. It details three new discoveries: Periodic Comets Kushida-Muramatsu and Wiseman-Skiff, and Comet McNaught-Russell, with the latter potentially reaching magnitude 11.5 in early April. The author also highlights the rare absence of visual comet discoveries in 1993.

articles.title: EPHEMERIDES
articles.summary: This document provides detailed ephemerides for three comets: Comet Mueller (1993p), Periodic Comet Shoemaker-Machmann 2, and Periodic Comet Shoemaker-Levy 9. For each comet, it lists celestial coordinates (Right Ascension, Declination), elongation, sky visibility, and apparent magnitude across various dates from late January through early March 1994. This information is essential for observers tracking these specific comets during the specified period.

articles.title: SAN JOSE ASTRONOMICAL ASSOCIATION MEMBERSHIP
articles.summary: This document outlines the submission guidelines for EPHEMERIS, the monthly publication of the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA). Members are encouraged to submit typed articles to editor Bob Madden by the 12th of the previous month, with a preference for text files on 3-1/2" IBM or MAC diskettes, though written submissions are also accepted.

articles.title: Membership only: $12 Membership / S&T: $32 Junior (under 18): $20
articles.summary: This document is a membership application form for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), outlining three types of memberships: Membership Only ($12), Membership with Sky & Telescope magazine ($32), and Junior (under 18) ($20). It provides fields for applicant information and instructions for submission to the treasurer, Jack Petersen.
